title: Lesson 2 Quiz: Opportunity Cost and Rational Decision-Making
description: A short quiz to check what you learned in this lesson. Submitting it meets the lesson's completion requirement (quiz submitted), and your score is recorded separately.

history.note: AI-written question draft. Not yet reviewed by a human (admin) and not to be given to students.
Rewritten in English from the Korean draft. Not reviewed or approved by a human.

questions.prompt: For 2 hours after school, you could (1) work a part-time job that pays $9 per hour, (2) go to a club activity, or (3) take a nap. You choose the club activity. If the job is worth more to you than the nap, what is the opportunity cost of the club activity?

choices.text: The rest you would have gotten from the nap
The $18 you could have earned at the job
The nap and the $18 from the job combined
Nothing, because you didn't spend any money

questions.prompt: You bought a non-refundable $60 amusement park day pass, but on the day of your visit it is raining and you feel a cold coming on. What is the most rational way to decide whether to go?

choices.text: Go, since using the $60 pass is the way to keep from wasting the money.
Check whether the $60 pass plus bus fare would be more than the fun of going.
Decide based on how many of your friends have already agreed to go along.
Compare today's fun with the risk of getting sick, leaving the pass price out.

questions.prompt: The value of the skill you gain from the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th hours of basketball practice (the marginal benefit) is $10, $8, $5, and $2, respectively. Each hour of practice gives up $6 worth of other activities (the marginal cost). If you practice only until the marginal benefit falls below the marginal cost, how many hours do you practice? (Enter a number only.)

A town can produce the following combinations of (loaves of bread, cakes): (0, 60), (10, 52), (20, 40), (30, 22), (40, 0). How many cakes are given up when bread production rises from 20 to 30 loaves? (Enter a number only.)
What does a point inside the production possibilities frontier represent?

choices.text: A combination that current resources and technology cannot produce
The combination of goods that society prefers over the others
An inefficient combination with idle workers or wasted resources
A combination at which the opportunity cost is equal to zero
